items.headline: AI debate has shifted from 'can we' to 'should we', IPG Autumn Conference 2026 hears
items.excerpt: AI was the dominant theme of the Independent Publishers Guild Autumn Conference on 10 September, across talks on ethics, licensing and audio. New IPG research shows adoption at 76% of indie publishers (vs 42% in 2023) and finds that "AI may have damaged trust more than it has changed workflows."

items.headline: Publishing's AI Reckoning
items.excerpt: PW's cover feature on how the book business is learning to live with generative AI, for better and worse: HarperCollins moving to automate overseas translation, Wiley booking $49M in AI licensing revenue in FY2026, and editorial teams absorbing AI into everyday production.

items.headline: Lost in Translation: AI comes for literary translators
items.excerpt: Tech developers argue automation will fundamentally reshape the craft of literary translation, pitching post-editing workflows to publishers. Translators push back, warning that machine drafts flatten voice and shift the job from authorship to cleanup.

items.headline: Ingram's AI Rollout Is a Success
items.excerpt: Fifteen months into deploying AI across its operations, Ingram says the technology is already changing how the distributor does business — from metadata and customer service to print-on-demand workflow decisions.

items.headline: Who Is Narrating the Future? AI and the Audiobook Market
items.excerpt: A new Frankfurter Buchmesse white paper produced by Dosdoce.com maps AI adoption in audiobook, audio drama and podcast production: 17% of respondents now use AI across more than six production phases, and 86% expect disruptive or moderate AI-driven growth within three years.

items.headline: Spotify's AI-powered audiobook narration opens up to all authors
items.excerpt: Spotify is opening its AI audiobook narration program to all authors, using ElevenLabs voice models to produce the audio at no cost and with no exclusivity requirement — a direct challenge to Audible/ACX economics for indie authors.

items.headline: Google rolls out AI chatbots for books, with permission from publishers and authors
items.excerpt: Google is shipping opt-in, per-title AI chat for books, letting readers question a text and generate infographics, audio overviews and quizzes from it — turning the reading surface itself into an interactive product publishers must design for.

items.headline: How good are AI custom-written novels?
items.excerpt: A close read of Ember Novels, which generates bespoke novels on demand: the system now carries plot across 300 pages with fewer continuity errors than many AI-assisted books already on the market, raising the floor for machine-made long-form fiction.

items.headline: Ask the Chefs: AI and Copyright Licensing
items.excerpt: After the US Department of Justice filed a Statement of Interest in NYT v. OpenAI/Microsoft largely siding with the AI companies on training-as-fair-use, publishing leaders weigh what a collapsing licensing premise means for rightsholders and content strategy.

items.headline: Guest Post — The Unbundling of Scholarly Publishing: A Trilemma for the AI Era
items.excerpt: The journal portfolio, platform or membership is no longer enough as AI rewires how research gets discovered and consumed. The authors lay out a trilemma publishers must choose within — and what product teams should rebuild first.

items.headline: We Can Now Track AI-Generated Content
items.excerpt: Provenance signals for AI text are now embedded in Claude models, giving editors a technical hook for detecting machine-written submissions. The post argues it doesn't solve publishing's disclosure problem and creates new ones.

items.headline: A new font promises to hide your text from AI
items.excerpt: Design studio Mixfont's Decoy Font renders text that humans can read but large language models cannot parse, pitched as a typographic defense against AI crawlers scraping writing and books.

items.headline: 50 Things Every AI Working With Humans Should Know — Ken Liu's machine-assisted story
items.excerpt: Lit Hub publishes Ken Liu's new story, written in explicit collaboration with AI systems and accompanied by an interview explaining the method — a rare documented craft record of literary co-writing rather than a disclosure scandal.

items.headline: What Machines Can't Replace: Why AI Makes Us More Human, with Anna McPhee
items.excerpt: Software engineer, author and creative technologist Anna McPhee walks through an author workflow that uses AI for research, editing, admin and marketing while every word of the book stays human-written — a concrete division-of-labour model for creative work.

items.headline: Plaintiffs File Motion for Summary Judgment v. OpenAI and Microsoft
items.excerpt: The Authors Guild and class plaintiffs filed their summary-judgment motion and brief in the consolidated In re OpenAI copyright MDL on 4 September, arguing training on pirated books cannot be fair use. (Note: adjacent to the Microsoft/Copilot MDL filing item covered 2026-09-07 — curator should check for overlap.)

items.headline: AI Updates, Remembering Dolly Parton, and More News for Library Workers
items.excerpt: Book Riot's library-worker roundup collects the week's AI developments touching collections and reading services — AI-generated ebook slop in catalogs, vendor AI features, and how library staff are being asked to vet machine-made titles.
